trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go up: left is number 7, which comes later.
Cell (5,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Cell (3,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going to number 3, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5). So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (up from number 2) was wrong, so the line must go right.

Going to number 3 would leave both cell (1,4) and cell (1,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
Cell (2,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going right would cut off the top-left corner (3 cells). So the line goes down.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going up would cut off the top-left corner (3 cells); going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going up would leave both cell (3,2) and cell (3,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes left.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (4,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
